records.request:
PR title: fix(init): isolate gc init from a parent .beads workspace

PR description:
v1.5.0 release blocker (rel15 validation finding F2; regression vs v1.4.2).

## Problem
A fresh `gc init` fails for any city created anywhere below a directory that already holds a bd workspace (a repo that uses beads, or a home with `~/.beads`):

```
Error: workspace already initialized as database "ws00", but --database "hq" was requested.
```

`gc rig add` of a rig below such a workspace fails the same way when the rig dir is not itself a git repo. v1.4.2 succeeded.

## Root cause
Since #6273, city/rig beads init goes through provider-owned `gc-beads-bd init` (`examples/bd/assets/scripts/gc-beads-bd.sh` `op_provider_owned_init`), which runs `bd init --init-if-missing ... --database <db>` with `BEADS_DIR=<scope>/.beads`. bd v1.3.0 (`internal/beads/beads.go` `FindBeadsDir`) honors `BEADS_DIR` only when that directory already contains a project file (metadata.json, config.yaml, dolt/, embeddeddolt/, *.db). For a fresh scope it falls back to the CWD walk-up, finds the ancestor workspace, and `--init-if-missing` aborts on the database mismatch. v1.4.2 ran `bd init --server` from `initDefaultRigBdStore` and swallowed "already initialized" (`isBdAlreadyInitializedError`), then wrote its own metadata, so it worked by accident. Without `--database`, bd would silently bind the new scope to the ancestor's store, so the loud failure is the lesser evil. The fix has to make `BEADS_DIR` authoritative.

## Fix
`op_provider_owned_init` anchors a fresh scope with an empty `.beads/config.yaml` (mode 600) before `bd init`. An empty config.yaml is the smallest project file that pins bd's resolution to the scope. bd init keeps an existing config.yaml instead of writing its comment-only template, and every setting it persists still lands in that file. If `bd init` fails, the script removes the anchor again (only while it is still the empty file the script wrote), because a leftover config.yaml reads as a persisted beads identity (`scopeHasPersistedBeadsIdentity`) and would misclassify the retry. Scopes that already have metadata.json, config.yaml, dolt/ or embeddeddolt/ are left alone.

Other bd-init call sites I checked:
- Legacy managed `op_init` (server/proxied): gc pre-seeds metadata.json before calling the script, so BEADS_DIR is already authoritative. I verified this with a real `gc init` plus `gc rig add` under an ancestor workspace: exit 0 both before and after this change.
- `op_init` doltlite branch and `initDefaultRigBdStore` (non-bd, non-exec providers only) have the same latent hazard. They are outside this scope and I filed them as a follow-up.
- `BdStore.Init` has no production callers.

## Tests
- `TestGcBeadsBdProviderOwnedInitAnchorsBeadsDirBeforeBdInit` (fake bd, fast): bd sees an empty config.yaml on fresh scopes (proxied and direct). The anchor is removed when bd init fails. An existing config.yaml is left untouched, including when init fails.
- `TestGcBeadsBdProviderOwnedRealInitIgnoresAncestorBeadsWorkspace` (real bd + dolt, slow tier): for both direct and proxied, `gc-beads-bd init` of a scope below an ancestor bd workspace succeeds. The scope metadata has `dolt_database=hq` and the correct `dolt_mode`, the ancestor metadata is unchanged, and `health` passes.
- Fail before / pass after: with the script restored from main, the three fresh-scope subtests fail (`bd init saw "config.yaml=missing"`) and both real subtests fail (`exit status 1`). With the fix, all pass. `go test ./cmd/gc -run 'GcBeadsBd|ProviderOwned|BeadsProvider|InitBeads|RigAdd'` and `go test ./examples/bd/...` pass.
- End-to-end with a real `gc init` (isolated HOME/GC_HOME, bd v1.3.0), comparing main with this change:
  - Ancestor workspace, proxied default: main exit 1, fix exit 0.
  - Ancestor workspace, direct: main exit 1, fix exit 0.
  - Ancestor workspace, proxied, parent not a git repo: main exit 1, fix exit 0.
  - `gc rig add` under an ancestor workspace, rig not a git repo: main exit 1, fix exit 0.
  - Legacy managed topology: exit 0 on both.
- Output equivalence: a city initialized under an ancestor with the fix and a city initialized in a clean directory have identical `.beads/config.yaml`, metadata (minus project_id), `types.custom`, `issue_prefix` and `bd create`, in both proxied and direct modes. The only differences are in the `bd context` git/repo-root lines, because the clean control dir is not a git repo.

## Risks
- A pre-created config.yaml is now present while bd init runs. bd v1.3.0 treats an existing config.yaml as "keep". A future bd that refuses to init over an existing config.yaml would break fresh init loudly, not silently.
- `TestGcBeadsBdProviderOwnedRealLifecycleStopsOwnedProcesses/direct` fails locally on this box with or without this change (pre-existing, environment-related).

records.request:
PR title: fix(beads): keep gc-owned proxied scopes out of bd's user-level shared server

PR description:
## Problem

v1.5.0 release blocker (packs-vs-RC finding F9, P1, silent data routing). On the proxied default (#6273), a user-level bd `dolt.shared-server: true` (in `~/.beads/config.yaml` or `~/.config/bd/config.yaml`, or `BEADS_DOLT_SHARED_SERVER=1`) silently moves gc-owned proxied city and rig stores into `~/.beads/shared-server`. That is one Dolt root for the whole host, so two cities' `hq` databases become one. This was seen live during the RC packs gate: two cities wrote into the same shared `hq`. v1.4.2 failed loudly in the same situation. Operators also can't work around it with a HOME override, because the supervisor refuses one.

## Root cause

bd reads `dolt.shared-server` through layered config: env, then the scope's `.beads/config.yaml`, then the user-level files. gc's proxied projection (`applyProxiedDoltEnv`, cmd/gc/bd_env.go ~1252) and the provider script (`run_provider_owned_bd` / `run_bd_init_proxied`, examples/bd/assets/scripts/gc-beads-bd.sh) never set the key. `bd init` also rewrites the scope's config.yaml, so under a user-level `true` it writes `dolt.shared-server: true` into the scope itself. That means pinning the value before init does not help.

## Fix

Everything below applies only to proxied scopes **gc owns**. A scope counts as gc-owned (`gcOwnsProxiedScope`) when it has an ownership-journal entry, a committed handoff, or gc's `gc.endpoint_origin` marker.

- **Scope pin.** After `bd init`, and on every `gc start`, gc writes `dolt.shared-server: false` into the scope's `.beads/config.yaml`. The start write happens before the provider start runs bd. This covers agents that run `bd` directly in their shell.
  - When the file has no `dolt` section, the pin is appended as text, so comments, blank lines and CRLF line endings survive byte for byte.
  - Otherwise the file is re-encoded with yaml.v3. CRLF is kept, but blank lines and extra spaces before comments are lost, and a flat `dolt.shared-server` key is folded into the nested form.
- **Env opt-out**: `BD_DOLT_SHARED_SERVER=false` (outranks every config file) plus `BEADS_DOLT_SHARED_SERVER=0` (cancels an inherited `1`). It is applied to:
  - bdRuntimeEnv for city and rig (controller, `gc bd`, orders, hooks);
  - agent session env;
  - the provider lifecycle env, only while a journaled proxied init is in flight (that env is city-wide and also serves rig operations);
  - the provider script, per scope: during a gc proxied init, or for a ready scope whose config.yaml carries gc's pin.
- **Found workspaces are left alone.** A proxied workspace gc merely found gets no env override and no rewrite, so gc's bd and an agent's bd always resolve it the same way. The same holds for external/bound and direct scopes.
- **New doctor check `proxied-shared-server`:**
  - error when a gc-owned scope is bound `true`;
  - warning when the user-level config enables shared-server mode and a scope has no pin;
  - warning while `${BEADS_SHARED_SERVER_DIR:-~/.beads/shared-server}/dolt/<scope db>` exists, because rows written while a scope was bound are stranded there and not migrated.
  - It skips scopes bd hasn't created yet and reports scopes whose ownership can't be classified. `--fix` writes the pin.
- **CI:** a new step in `beads-topology-acceptance` runs `TestBeadsProxiedIgnoresUserLevelSharedServer`, the job cap moves from 90 to 105 minutes, the cipolicy hash is bumped, and the resource ledger goes up by one bd call.

## Tests

- Unit: `internal/beads/contract` (pin read/write, comment-preserving, flat-key cleanup), `internal/doctor` (check states, user-level resolution with injected env/home), and `cmd/gc` (runtime, provider and session env; the pin only for owned scopes; skipped for unmaterialized scopes; the provider script on Linux).
- Fail-before/pass-after: with the opt-out and pin removed, `TestProxiedRuntimeEnvPinsBdSharedServerOff`, `TestProviderScriptPinsSharedServerOffForProxiedScopes`, `TestEnsureGCOwnedProxiedScopeSharedServerOff` and `TestSessionEnvPinsBdSharedServerOffForGCOwnedProxiedScopes` fail. With the fix they pass.
- End-to-end repro through gc (fake HOME with `shared-server: true`, bd v1.3.0):
  - RC gc: `gc init` binds the city into `$HOME/.beads/shared-server` (no `city/.beads/dolt`, `hq` created in the shared root).
  - This branch: the city has its own `.beads/dolt`, the shared root is empty, the scope config is pinned, and a raw `bd create` with no gc env stays local.
- Acceptance `TestBeadsProxiedIgnoresUserLevelSharedServer` (acceptance_a; user config via XDG_CONFIG_HOME, shared dir redirected with BEADS_SHARED_SERVER_DIR, never the real ~/.beads). Locally, all the store, sidecar, pin and raw-bd assertions pass for the city and the rig. The `proxied-shared-server` doctor check reports ok.

records.request:
PR title: fix(core): skip reaper and jsonl-export on bd-owned proxied cities

PR description:
**v1.5.0 release blocker (P1, packs-vs-rc F5).**

## Problem
New cities have defaulted to bd-owned proxied Dolt since #6273 (`.beads/metadata.json` `dolt_mode=proxied-server`). On those cities the core `reaper` order (30m) and the `jsonl-export` order (15m) fail on every run with exit 78 `gc dolt: cannot resolve runtime port`. As a result, wisps are never reaped, closed molecules are never purged, and no JSONL archive is written. Each cooldown also adds another `OrderFailed`. v1.4.2 does not have this problem: it used gc-managed Dolt, so `dolt-state.json` existed. This is a regression.

## Root cause
- `internal/bootstrap/packs/core/assets/scripts/dolt-target.sh:158-186` (pre-fix): `core_city_has_dolt_target()` finds `.beads/dolt` and says "yes". The script then calls `resolve_dolt_port_or_die`, which exits 78 because the city has no gc-managed state file and no `GC_DOLT_PORT`.
- `cmd/gc/order_store.go:287-297`: for a proxied scope, `canonicalScopeDoltTarget` returns `!ok`, so no port is projected. This is intentional (`cmd/gc/bd_env_proxied.go`: "resolves no host or port for a local upstream — bd's proxy owns that listener").

## Why skip rather than resolve the proxy endpoint
Pointing these scripts at the proxy's Dolt child is not safe:
- bd owns the proxied Dolt child, its lifecycle and its idle semantics. `engdocs/design/beads-proxied-local-default.md` lists "Native SQL over the proxy" as deliberately not done; the follow-ups are ga-p9iuv.42-.46.
- gc's own proxied native handle is read-only by construction (`OpenNativeDoltStoreAtProxied`: "No native write reaches a bd-owned database"). bd v1.3.0 refuses `dolt commit` in proxied mode.
- `reaper.sh` issues UPDATE/DELETE statements followed by `CALL DOLT_COMMIT`.
- Both scripts run `SHOW DATABASES` against a single server and assume it holds every scope's database. Under proxied mode each scope (the city and every rig) has its own child.

## Fix
`dolt-target.sh` now sources the dolt pack's existing `proxied_scope.sh` and uses `bd_owns_proxied_scope`. That function is the shell twin of `scopeBindingIsProviderOwnedProxied`, and `examples/bd/dolt/proxied_scope_test.go` already pins the two to agree. The dolt pack uses it today to turn its own managed-Dolt verbs into typed no-ops. On a bd-owned proxied city the script prints `core: city Dolt is bd-owned (dolt_mode=proxied-server); direct-SQL maintenance is not supported on proxied scopes; skipping <script>` and exits 0.

The check runs before the `GC_DOLT_PORT` shortcut. That way a port projected for a proxied scope's external upstream also cannot send raw SQL around bd's proxy. Legacy gc-managed cities are unchanged.

I checked the other core scripts. `reaper.sh` and `jsonl-export.sh` are the only ones that source `dolt-target.sh`. The rest go through `gc bd` / bd.

## Tests
`examples/gastown` `TestMaintenanceDoltScriptsSkipBdOwnedProxiedCity` runs both scripts against four cases:
- proxied, no port → skips with exit 0; Dolt and gc are never invoked
- proxied, with a projected port → skips with exit 0
- legacy managed (`dolt_mode=server`), no runtime state → still exits 78
- legacy managed, with a projected port → dials `--port 4406`

Before the fix, all 4 proxied subtests fail. After the fix, all 8 subtests pass.

Also passing: `go test ./examples/gastown ./examples/bd/dolt ./internal/bootstrap/...` and `go vet`.

## Risks / known gap
On proxied cities the reaper (including its closed-session-bead prune steps) and the JSONL export still do not run. What changed is that they now skip cleanly with a clear line instead of failing every cooldown. Proxied scopes also have no Dolt backup (bd refuses `backup*`). The follow-up is to port both orders to bd front-door verbs: `bd export`, and `bd sql` / `bd purge` / `bd prune`.

Refs packs-vs-rc F5, #6273.

records.title: fix(gc): purge closed session beads from the sqlite infra ledger
records.request:
PR title: fix(gc): purge closed session beads from the sqlite infra ledger

PR description:
v1.5.0 release blocker. Carries the owner's (@julianknutsen) two original commits unchanged, with authorship kept:

- `cf8b925697` fix(gc): purge closed session beads from the sqlite infra ledger
- `042763cd9a` fix(gc): keep closed sqlite sessions for 3 days, not 30

A third commit fixes the review findings on top of them.

## Problem
On a split city, agent sessions (`gcg-session-*`, `gcs-*`) live in the SQLite infra ledger. Reaper step 6 queries the Dolt work database and can't see them, so closed sessions pile up there with no limit. The owner's commits add a wisp-GC arm that deletes closed `type=session` beads once they have been idle past `GC_INFRA_SESSION_PURGE_AGE` (default 72h). The Dolt reaper's `GC_REAPER_SESSION_PURGE_AGE` stays a separate clock at 720h, unchanged.

## Root cause of the review blocker
As first written, the arm ran on `graphStore.Store` (`cmd/gc/wisp_gc.go`, runGC). The controller passes `cr.graphBeadStore()` (`cmd/gc/city_runtime.go` wisp GC phase), which goes through `resolveClassStore` (`cmd/gc/class_store.go`). When the routes don't relocate a class, that function hands back the **work store**, and that is the case for every unsplit city (`storageSplitNone`, `cmd/gc/storage_boot.go`). So with wisp GC enabled, the arm would delete closed sessions straight out of the Dolt work store. None of step 6's guards applied (pattern, backup age, anomaly threshold), and disabling the reaper order would not have stopped it.

## Fix (commit 3)
- **Relocation gate, on the sessions class.** `runGC` now takes the sessions-class store as its own argument. The controller builds it with `CityRuntime.infraSessionLedger()` → `relocatedSQLiteSessionLedger(routes, sessionsBeadStore(), workStore)`. It is non-nil only when all of these hold:
  - the routes relocate `ClassSessions`;
  - the resolved sessions store is that routed `*beads.SQLiteStore`;
  - that store is not the work store.

  In every other case the arm does nothing: no routes, sessions left on work, a Dolt workspace binding, or a refused binding. The arm targets `sessionsBeadStore()`, not the graph store.
- **Explicit trigger.** The arm runs only when `wisp_ttl > 0` (the graph-class GC is on) and a ledger was handed over. A GC that is enabled only by `[mail] retention_ttl` does not purge session history.
- **Re-read before delete.** Each candidate is re-read with `Get` right before `Delete`. It is skipped unless it is still `type=session`, still closed, and still past the cutoff. This closes the reopen race (`reopenClosedConfiguredNamedSessionBead`).
- **Bounded scan.** The list pushes `UpdatedBefore` down to the store and examines at most 2000 candidates per tick; kept candidates count toward that budget. Deletes stay capped at 500. A `(created_at, id)` cursor on the tracker resumes after the last examined candidate and resets once the list is exhausted, so sessions that still hold children don't starve the rest of the backlog.
- **Housekeeping.** `GC_INFRA_SESSION_PURGE_AGE` is added to `internal/testenv/testdata/gc_env_read_baseline.golden`; the owner named the variable, so this is a deliberate golden update. The one `routes.storeFor` gate site carries a `residency:allow` annotation because it resolves no bead.
- **Unchanged.** Workflow steps, open sessions, and sessions with parent-child children or dep edges are never deleted. `GC_INFRA_SESSION_PURGE_AGE` falls back to 72h when unset, invalid, zero, or negative. There is no periodic VACUUM. The reaper.sh edit is comment-only and documents the gate and the two separate clocks.

## Tests
Owner's tests plus new ones, all in `cmd/gc/wisp_gc_test.go`:
- `TestWispGC_UnsplitCitySessionPurgeLeavesWorkStore`: runGC-level on a real SQLite *work* store in three unsplit shapes (no routes, routes that leave sessions on work, sessions routed at the work store itself). The GC collects a closed molecule, which proves it ran, but the old closed session survives.
- `TestWispGC_SplitCityPurgesClosedInfraSessions`: whole-split routes onto a SQLite ledger.
  - A GC with mail retention only purges nothing.
  - With `wisp_ttl` set, 4-day-old closed `gcg-session-*`/`gcs-*` beads are purged on the 72h clock. The 2-day-old, open, and child-holding sessions and the child are kept.
  - The work store sees zero deletes.
- `TestRelocatedSQLiteSessionLedgerRequiresSQLite`, `TestInfraSessionPurgeAgeEnv` (the fallbacks; `GC_REAPER_SESSION_PURGE_AGE` doesn't move it), `TestPurgeClosedInfraSessionsSkipsSessionReopenedBeforeDelete`, `TestWispGC_SessionPurgeScanBudgetDoesNotStarve` (per-tick purges `[0 1 1]` behind 3 held sessions with a scan budget of 2; cursor resets).
- Fail-before: with the gate and re-read reverted to the owner's behaviour, the unsplit, mail-only and reopen tests fail ("closed session on the work store was purged", "mail-retention-only GC purged a session", "purged = 2, want 1").
- Commands run: `go test -count=1 -run 'TestPurgeClosedInfraSessions|TestWispGC_PurgesExpiredMolecules|TestWispGC_NothingExpired|…' ./cmd/gc` and the focused `WispGC|Wisp|Reap|Purge|InfraClass|ClassStore|StorageRoutes|Reaper` sweep all pass. `go vet`, gofmt and golangci-lint (new from main) are clean. The full pre-push `test-fast-parallel` suite passed.
- Fixtures only. No reaper or wisp GC was run against a live city or Dolt 3307, and the maintainer-city reaper stays disabled.

## Risks
- `runGC` has a new parameter. All callers and test doubles are updated.
- `SeekAfter` resolves in Go, so SQLite decodes every closed session older than the cutoff each tick. Only the probes and deletes are bounded. This costs little on SQLite, and the arm never runs on Dolt.
- There is still a small window between the re-read and the `Delete`, because the store has no conditional delete and the arm takes no identifier lock. Controller-originated reopens are serialized with the tick.
- `GC_INFRA_SESSION_PURGE_AGE` is [truncated]

records.request:
PR title: fix: make mail archive repair open messages

PR description:
## Problem

`gc mail archive <id>` can report "already archived" for a message that is still open. The message then stays in the unread inbox, and `gc hook` keeps routing it to the recipient.

`beadmail.Provider.Archive` looked the message up with `store.Get(id)` and treated `ErrNotFound` as "already archived". Behind the caching store, `Get` can report a bead as missing when it still exists: it answers `ErrNotFound` from the cache's own record of recent mutations without reading the backing store again. An open message the cache has lost track of therefore reads as gone. Archive returns `ErrAlreadyArchived` and never closes it.

## Fix

Archive now looks the id up with a `List` that reads the backing store directly (`Live: true`), searches both store tiers (`TierBoth`), and includes closed rows. It only reports "already archived" when that lookup returns nothing. The rest of the function is unchanged: an already-closed message still returns `ErrAlreadyArchived` without mutation, a missing id still returns `ErrAlreadyArchived`, and a non-message bead is still an error.

## Tests

- New `TestArchiveRepairsOpenMessageMissingFromDirectLookup` reproduces the miss: an open message that direct lookup does not return. It asserts that archive succeeds, the bead ends closed, the recipient's open-assignee hook input is empty, and the unread inbox is empty.
- The new test fails with `Archive: already archived` when the fix hunk is reverted, and passes with it restored.
- Existing idempotency coverage still passes: 15 `cmd/gc` archive tests (missing id, already closed, non-message, batch and filtered selection) and the API repeat-archive test.

PR title: fix: protect beads initialization during concurrent migrations

PR description:
Concurrent `gc init` calls sharing a Dolt database can mistake a database with no beads tables yet for an empty store and run a second forced initialization over an active migration. This change treats an active migration cursor or retained migration history as existing state, waits while the cursor continues advancing, and refuses a destructive reinitialization when that state does not settle.

Forced initialization now takes a database-specific advisory lock and rechecks emptiness after acquiring it. This closes both the classification-to-force race and the race between separate initializer processes sharing a Dolt database.

records.request:
PR title: fix(bd): serve gc bd show --watch in proxied mode

PR description:
## Problem
v1.5.0 release blocker (owner rc1 gate): `gc bd show <id> --watch` fails on every default v1.5.0 city with `Error: watch mode not supported in proxied-server mode` (exit 1). Tutorial 01 and the quickstart use it, and RC Gate's `TestTutorial01Cities/PrimaryWizardFlow/gc_bd_show_mp-ff9_--watch` failed on it (runs 36235599985 and 36235611581). #6676 worked around this in the docs by telling users to re-run `gc bd show`. The owner wants a product fix before rc1.

## Root cause
- #6273 (af7ad8a0fe) made bd-owned proxied-server Dolt the default transport.
- beads v1.3.0 refuses watch for `show` in that mode: `cmd/bd/proxy_capability.go:229` (`proxyCommandCapabilities["show"]` → `proxy.watch.unsupported`). The check runs in `validateProxyCapabilitiesBeforeProvider` (`proxy_capability.go:337-340`) and again in `runShowProxiedServer` (`show_proxied_server.go:97-99`).
- `gc bd` (cmd/gc/cmd_bd.go `doBd`) forwarded `--watch` to bd as-is.
- bd is pinned at v1.3.0 and bd can never call gc, so the fix has to be on the gc side.
- Other watch commands: `bd list --watch` is **honored** in proxied mode (`proxy_capability.go:230`), and `show` is the only bd verb with a refused `--watch`. No change is needed for any other command.

## Fix
- New `cmd/gc/cmd_bd_show_watch.go`, hooked into `doBd` just before the bd exec. It applies when argv is `show <exactly one id> --watch|-w` (no `--as-of` or `--current`) **and** the scope is proxied (`scopeUsesProxiedDoltMode`, or `BEADS_DOLT_PROXIED_SERVER` truthy in the projected env). In that case gc serves the watch the way bd's own `watchIssue` does (`cmd/bd/show_display.go:32`):
  - render with plain `bd show <args minus --watch>`, so bd still owns the output format
  - poll `bd show --json --id=<id>` every 2s (bd's interval) and redraw when `id:status:updated_at` changes (bd's snapshot key)
  - print bd's own `Watching for changes... (Press Ctrl+C to exit)` and `Stopped watching.` lines on stderr
  - exit 0 on Ctrl+C or SIGTERM
  - if the first render fails, return bd's exit code
  - bd subprocesses use the same binary, directory and environment as the passthrough.
- Non-proxied scopes: `--watch` still goes straight to bd, unchanged.
- The `gc bd --help` text documents the exception (docs/reference/cli.md regenerated).
- Docs and golden: the `--watch` step is restored in tutorial 01, the tutorial golden and the command manifest. This reverts #6676's watch wording and keeps its `[imports.gc]` fixes. The quickstart and `examples/lifecycle` now say `gc bd show <bead-id> --watch` (raw `bd show --watch` stays refused by bd on proxied cities).

## Tests
- `TestParseBdShowWatchArgs`: which argv forms gc serves and which it leaves to bd.
- `TestRunBdShowWatchRedrawsOnChangeAndStopsOnCancel`: exactly one render while the bead is unchanged, one redraw on change, exit 0 plus `Stopped watching.` on cancel.
- `TestRunBdShowWatchReturnsInitialRenderFailure`: bd's exit code is returned when the first render fails.
- `TestGcBdShowWatchIsServedByGCOnProxiedScope`: `doBd` on a proxied city, with a fake bd that refuses `--watch` the way v1.3.0 does. The bead renders, redraws when status changes and stops on cancel, and bd never receives `--watch`. **Before the fix it fails** (the bead never renders because the fake bd refuses; verified by disabling the hook). After the fix it passes.
- `TestGcBdShowWatchPassesThroughOnNonProxiedScope`: a managed direct scope sends `show mp-1 --watch` to bd unchanged.
- Manual end-to-end with a real bd v1.3.0 built from the pinned module, on a `bd init --proxied-server` scope. Raw `bd show mp-174 --watch` still fails with `watch mode not supported in proxied-server mode`. `gc bd show mp-174 --watch` rendered the bead, redrew `IN_PROGRESS` → `OPEN` after a `bd update`, and printed `Stopped watching.` on SIGINT.
- Local runs: `go test ./cmd/gc -run 'Bd|ShowWatch|Proxied'` ok, `go test -tags acceptance_c ./test/acceptance/tutorial_goldens -run TestTutorialCommandInventoryMatchesPinnedDocs` ok, `go vet`, `make lint-changed` (0 issues), `make check-docs` ok, `make bazel-sync`.

## Risks
- Each poll spawns one `bd show --json`. On a proxied scope that costs a proxy round trip, roughly the cost bd's own in-process poll would have. Slow polls just skip ticks.
- Like bd, changes are detected from `status` and `updated_at` only. A comment-only change does not redraw, which is also how bd behaves.
- If bd's `--json` shape changes, the snapshot falls back to the raw JSON bytes, so gc redraws on any change rather than missing one.
- Raw `bd show --watch` (without `gc`) is still refused on proxied cities. That is a beads limitation. The work-lifecycle diagram artwork still says `bd show <id> --watch`.

Refs #6273, #6676, ga-043xs. v1.5.0 release blocker (rc1 gate). Backport together with #6676.

## Problem
#4508 made `gc init` import the public Gas City pack as `[imports.gc]`, but every city created by gc v1.4.x has `[imports.gascity]`, and nothing moves them over. The import key namespaces the pack's skills and commands, so those cities get `gascity.mayor` instead of `gc.mayor` today. Once they bump the pack past 0.1.6, role prompts that run `gc gc claim` fail with `unknown command "gc"`.

## Root cause
The binding is stamped on imported skills/commands/agents (`internal/config/pack.go`, BindingName). `config.GascityCityWithProviders` (internal/config/config.go:~4592) now writes `gc`. Nothing rewrites existing keys: not init, not `doctor --fix`, not the import-state migrations (cmd/gc/import_state_doctor_check.go only handles gastown/maintenance).

## Fix
New `gascity-pack-binding` doctor check (`cmd/gc/gascity_pack_binding_doctor_check.go`), registered after `packv2-import-state`:
- **Detect**: looks at the city pack's root imports (pack.toml `[imports]` plus city.toml root `[imports]` overrides; `gc init` writes pack.toml). It identifies the pack by source layout via `builtinpacks.SourceLayout`, so any spelling of gascity-packs `//gascity` matches (tree URL, `.git//gascity`, trailing slash) and the key name plays no part. The gc-roles subpack, gastown, and third-party packs don't match. Rig imports and `[defaults.rig.imports]` are never read for rewrite. Severity: **warning**.
- **--fix**: renames the key to `gc` in place with the manifest helpers `gc import add/remove` use (`loadCityPackManifestFS`/`writeCityPackManifest`, `writeCityImportManifestFS`), carrying the whole `config.Import` over. It snapshots both files and rolls back if a write fails. `packs.lock` is keyed by source, so it stays byte-identical (verified). Idempotent.
- **Refuses (no write, explains)** when:
  - `gc` is already bound to a different source.
  - A second Gas City import differs from `gc` in source spelling, version, or knobs.
  - pack.toml or city.toml references `<key>.`-qualified names (for example a patch on `gascity.x`).
- An exact duplicate of `gc` (same source+version+knobs) is removed. This is the "README `--name gc` next to the old `gascity`" case.
- Formatting: the repo's TOML writer re-encodes pack.toml (indentation, no comments), the same as `gc import add`.

Docs: new troubleshooting section for the check. understanding-packs.md and pack-spec.md examples now use `[imports.gc]` / `gc.planner`.

- v1.4-style city (`[imports.gascity]` plus rig `[rigs.imports.gascity]` plus `[defaults.rig.imports.gc]` roles):

  - city.toml is untouched and packs.lock is unchanged.
  - A second run is OK, and a second fix is byte-idempotent.
  - `LoadWithIncludes` gives the same agents and formulas before and after, with skill `gascity.mayor` becoming `gc.mayor`.
- The full `doctor.Run(fix=true)` loop reports it as fixed.
- Conflicting `gc` key: no change, and the error names the other source.
- Duplicate same-source `gc`: removed. Duplicate with a different version: refused.
- Third-party pack as `gascity`, gastown, and roles as root imports: untouched.
- A city.toml root override using the `.git//gascity` spelling is renamed.
- Binding-qualified reference: refused.
- Source-identity table.
- `doctor_check_names.golden` updated.

records.request:
PR title: fix(orders): keep redacted condition-check stderr so a broken check is distinguishable from a false one

PR description:
## Summary

A condition trigger runs its check command with stderr sent to `io.Discard`. When the check exits non-zero, `gc order check` shows either `condition: not met (exit 1)` or `check command failed: exit status 1`, and nothing else. A script that ran and answered "no" looks the same as a script that could not run at all.

This PR keeps a bounded, redacted tail of the check's stderr and puts it in the reason:

- Non-zero exit with empty stderr is unchanged: `condition: not met (exit N)`.
- Non-zero exit with stderr becomes `check command failed: exit status N: stderr: <excerpt>`.
- The excerpt comes from the last 4096 bytes of stderr. If earlier output was dropped, it starts at the next full line. It is folded onto one line, control and non-printing characters are replaced, and it is capped at 300 runes.
- Redaction runs before truncation. Values of sensitive environment variables (`execenv.IsSensitiveKey`) are replaced with the redaction marker, including values of one to three bytes, which `execenv.RedactText` skips. The capture buffer grows by the length of the longest such value, so a secret that straddles the 4096-byte cut is still whole when it is redacted.
- `TriggerResult` gains a `TimedOut` field. The dispatcher's "raise check_timeout" log line used to fire on `strings.Contains(reason, "timed out")`, so stderr containing those words would have been reported as a timeout. It now reads the field.

## Test plan

- `internal/orders/triggers_test.go`: 12 new cases covering stderr in the reason, the byte and rune caps, line-boundary trimming, control and non-printing characters, redaction of sensitive values (including a multi-line secret across the tail boundary and values shorter than four bytes), and a failure whose stderr says "timed out" not being marked as a timeout.
- `cmd/gc/order_dispatch_test.go`: a condition failure whose stderr mentions "timed out" does not produce the check_timeout log line.
- The two redaction regressions fail with the fix reverted and pass with it.
- `make test` at `ad4abe6e12`: 47480 passed, 0 failed, 224 skipped. `go build`, `go vet`, `golangci-lint` and `go test -race ./cmd/gc -run 'ManagedDolt|DoltRecovery|DoltState'` clean.

PR description:
## Problem
v1.5.0 release blocker (final pre-rc1 RC Gate runs 36235599985 / 36235611581 on release/v1.5.0 @ 4b55f28293). Three test-only failures, none a product regression:

1. **ubuntu / fast tests / unit-core**: `internal/events` reported `FAIL` after `PASS` with `testing: can't write .../testlog.txt: ... file too large`.
2. **Mac integration packages / core**: `TestNativeDoltStoreMetadataMergeSurvivesAConcurrentUpdateLoop/embedded/issues` (P0-6 stress test, #6233): `SetMetadataBatch gave up on 20 of 60 calls (33%), want at most 25%`. Zero lost keys.
3. **Mac integration packages / core**: every `TestSSHConformance` subtest (#6278): `ssh start "gc-test-conform-N": tmux new-session exited 1`.

## Root cause and fix
1. `internal/events/recorder_shortwrite_unix_test.go:37` lowered the **process-wide** `RLIMIT_FSIZE` to 5 bytes inside the test binary. Any other file write while that limit was in force failed with EFBIG, including the go test harness's buffered `-test.testlogfile` flush. The error is sticky, so the package failed. **Fix:** run the rlimit half in a child copy of the test binary (`GC_EVENTS_SHORTWRITE_HELPER=1`). The parent checks the child's result and skips when the child reports that the kernel did not short-write. The assertion itself is unchanged.
2. `internal/beads/native_dolt_store_metadata_stress_integration_test.go:26`: the 25% give-up bound depends on host scheduling. `SetMetadataBatch` has a 3-attempt budget, and a refusal is surfaced, never lost. **Fix:** raise the sanity ceiling to 50%. The lost-update assertions stay strict (zero successful writes may be missing). I measured whether the rate can detect a retry that stops re-reading: a mutation that re-used the first read on every retry gave up on only 2-27% of calls on Linux, which overlaps the correct implementation's 0-33%. So the rate is not that proof, at 25% or at 50%. The scripted interleavings (`TestNativeDoltStoreSetMetadataBatchKeepsAConcurrentUpdateAgainstRealDolt` / `...OnAWisp`) fail deterministically on that mutation. The comment now says this.
3. `internal/runtime/ssh/conformance_integration_test.go:104`: the fixture set `TMUX_TMPDIR` to `t.TempDir()`. On macOS that path is nested under `/var/folders/...` plus the subtest name, so `$TMUX_TMPDIR/tmux-<uid>/default` overran the 104-byte Unix socket cap and the tmux server never started. **Fix:** use `testutil.ShortTempDir` (rooted at /tmp on darwin).

- beads: `go test -tags integration ./internal/beads -run 'TestNativeDoltStoreMetadataMergeSurvivesAConcurrentUpdateLoop'`, 3 runs, 0-27% give-ups, PASS. Mutation results are listed above.

## Risks
Test-only. For (2), the reviewer should confirm that a 50% ceiling plus strict lost-key checks plus the scripted re-read proofs is an acceptable split. Separate product observation (bead ga-559u1): on the Mac runner, a third of contended `SetMetadataBatch` calls return ErrVersionMismatch after 3 attempts. The error is surfaced, not lost, but callers see it.

PR title: fix: fence suspended rig workers at spawn and claim

PR description:
## Summary

A suspended rig could still get pool workers spawned into it, and those workers then failed `gc hook --claim` with a bare exit 1 (`gc hook: agent "<rig>/<agent>" is suspended`). They could neither claim work nor drain cleanly, because the error path skipped the requested `--drain-ack` and each worker needed a manual `gc runtime drain-ack`. The status commands also disagreed about what was suspended. `gc rig list` reported the rig suspended, while `gc agent list` reported its agent not suspended.

This PR closes both ends of that split:

- **Spawn fence.** The start path re-checks rig suspension immediately before `Start` (`cmd/gc/session_lifecycle_parallel.go`). A suspended rig gets no new session. If the suspension state cannot be read, the start fails closed.
- **Claim fence.** `gc hook --claim` from a suspended city, rig or agent now returns a normal drain result with a reason (`city_suspended`, `rig_suspended`, `agent_suspended`) instead of an error. A worker that was already running when its rig was suspended drains the same way it does for any other drain reason.
- **Reporting.** `gc status` and `gc agent` attribute a rig-level suspension to the rig, not to the agent (`cmd_status.go`, `cmd_agent.go`, `cmd_suspend.go`).

## Contract change

`schemas/hook/result.schema.json` gains three values in the drain `reason` enum: `city_suspended`, `agent_suspended`, `rig_suspended`. The new values only widen the enum, but any consumer that validates against a closed copy of the schema will need them. I'd like a maintainer to confirm the contract change before merge.

## Related open PRs

These fix other suspension leaks and don't overlap with this diff:

- #6567 stops the seat-claim backstop and named-session materialization from waking a suspended agent.
- #4001 stops the reconciler from preserving a suspended rig's named sessions.

PR title: perf(lint): bound golangci-lint with GOMEMLIMIT so a full run fits beside another job

PR description:
## Summary

`golangci-lint run ./...` peaks at about 10.6 GiB resident on this repo. On a host where several agents share a memory-capped slice, one lint plus one `go test ./...` does not fit, and the lint gets OOM-killed along with whatever else is in the slice.

This PR sets `GOMEMLIMIT` on every golangci-lint invocation in the Makefile (`lint-full`, `lint-new`, `lint-changed`, `lint-affected`, `fmt-check`, `fmt-check-changed`, `fmt`). The default is 6GiB, set through a new `LINT_GOMEMLIMIT` variable. `LINT_GOMEMLIMIT=off` removes the cap. `0` is a zero-byte limit, not "off".

Matched cold runs (golangci-lint cache cleaned before each) on the same tree at default concurrency, golangci-lint 2.9.0:

| run | peak RSS | wall clock | issues |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| unbounded | 11,135,932 KB | 1:43 | 0 |
| `GOMEMLIMIT=6GiB` | 6,296,836 KB | 2:03 | 0 |

The cap costs about 20 seconds per full run.

`--concurrency` does not bound the memory. With `--concurrency 4` the run was above 10.86 GiB and still climbing at 2:12 when it was killed, because most of the memory is the loaded package and type graph for `./...`, which every worker shares.

The recipes now share one `LINT_ENV` variable that carries both the read-only `GOFLAGS` and `GOMEMLIMIT`. `scripts/lint_readonly_contract_test.go` checks the recipe text, so it is updated to match, and a new `TestLintTargetsApplyMemoryLimit` pins the cap at all seven sites.

## Test plan

- `go test ./scripts/`: the updated read-only checks and the new memory-limit check pass. Deleting `GOMEMLIMIT` from `LINT_ENV` or from `lint-changed` makes them fail.
- `make lint` at this head: 0 issues.

PR description:

When `sessionOwnsLiveClaim` found the claimed bead but the claim was not held (closed, released or re-owned), it kept walking the other residency legs. records.request:
PR title: fix(sessions): never drain a new pool worker that holds a live claim (rc1 slice)

PR description:
**v1.5.0 release blocker** (Tier C FreshInit first-run drain). This is the owner-approved rc1 slice.

## Problem
On a fresh `gc init` + `gc sling`, the first claude pool worker is often drained with `Draining session 'claude-…': orphaned` 3-20s after it claims its `do-work` step. RC Gate FreshInit shards fail intermittently: 3/4 on bb47a7d25b, and 3/16 on base 70cc5ed142 in the bisect. So this is pre-existing and load-dependent, not a regression.

## Root cause
1. **The post-create floor is lost** (`cmd/gc/session_lifecycle_parallel.go`, `commitStartResultTraced`, `ConfirmState: confirmPendingStart(state)`).
   - The reconciler heal pass writes `state=awake` before the async start commit lands.
   - `confirmPendingStart` excludes `awake`, so the commit never stamps `state_reason=creation_complete`.
   - `poolSessionWithinPostCreateProtection` requires that marker. The recovery path (`recoverRunningPendingCreate`) already confirmed from awake.
2. **The claim makes demand vanish.** The claim moves the step to in_progress under assignee `claude`. The cached in_progress pass (up to ~60s stale) cannot see it, and neither can the assignee-spelling guard on the not-desired arm (`sessionHasOpenAssignedWorkForConfigInfo`). As a result `poolDesired` drops and the orphaned arm drains the worker. No drain decider read `current_claim_bead_id`.
3. **An orphaned drain could not be revised.** Once an "orphaned" drain had begun, a claim that became visible a tick later could not cancel it.

Full history and the design are in the release research (`history-orphan-claim.md`, epic ga-uvzj6).

## Fix
- **(a)** A new `confirmStartCommitState` = `confirmPendingStart(s) || s == awake`. Both commit paths use it. `StartsAwakeInterval` stays keyed on `confirmPendingStart`, so an in-flight awake interval is never reset.
- **(b)** A new file `cmd/gc/session_ownership.go`, the seed of the v1.6 shared never-stop-an-owner predicate (ga-uvzj6). `sessionOwnsLiveClaim` works like this:
  - It does a **live** read of the session bead's `current_claim_bead_id`, through `beads.HandlesFor(store).Live`, not the cache.
  - It then does a live read of the claimed bead through the same residency legs the assigned-work guards use.
  - The claim counts as held while that bead is not closed. **Any read error counts as held.**
  - A claim is not held if the bead is back in the queue (open and unassigned), or if its `gc.session_id` names another session. This fence is for stale stamps (#6110).
  - `liveClaimVetoApplies` limits the veto to pool sessions whose agent is still configured and not suspended (agent, rig or city), so config removal and suspension still stop the session.
  - It is wired into the not-desired **orphaned** drain and the **no-wake-reason / idle** drain. The veto is logged once per (session, claim).
- **(c)** `liveClaimDrainReasonCancelable` covers only "orphaned". An in-flight reconciler-owned orphaned drain is cancelled once the live claim is seen. This covers both the tracked drain and a published reconciler drain ack, on the not-desired and desired drain-ack arms. Deliberate drains keep their current behaviour: config-drift, suspended, execution-stalled, user-hold, max-age and config removal.
- **(d)** A separate commit adds `TestFreshInit_SlingSpawnsDefaultPoolWorker` and `TestFreshInit_ClaudeUnrestricted` to the Nightly tier-c `-run` selector.
  - Nightly already has the same `OLLAMA_API_KEY` secret and model vars that RC Gate uses.
  - The reviewed cipolicy nightly hash is updated.

## Tests
- `TestOwnershipVetoAcrossDeciders` is a decider table test that future deciders will extend.
  - Deciders (5): orphaned begin, orphaned in flight (tracked), orphaned in flight (acked), no-wake-reason, idle.
  - Ownership variants (8), run against a primed CachingStore whose backing store takes the out-of-process claim:
    - kept: live claim with a stale cache, claim read error;
    - drained: no claim, claim bead closed, claim released, claim owned by another session, agent removed from config, agent suspended.
  - The drained variants are asserted to stop with the exact expected reason.
- `TestCommitStartResult_HealedAwakeBeforeCommitStillConfirmsCreation` covers the exact race. It checks for `creation_complete`, that the worker is within post-create protection, and that `awake_started_at` is preserved.
- Other new tests:
  - `TestOwnershipVeto_InFlightOrphanedDrainCancelledWhenClaimAppears` (tick 1 drains, then the claim lands, then tick 2 cancels);
  - `_DeliberateInFlightDrainsNotCancelled`, `_UserHoldDrainUnaffected`, `_MaxSessionAgeUnaffected`, `_LogsOnce`;
  - `TestSessionOwnsLiveClaim`, `TestLiveClaimDrainReasonCancelable`, `TestConfirmStartCommitState`.
- **Fail before / pass after:** I neutralised the fix (veto gate forced false; commit confirm without awake). Every "kept" table row failed, as did the healed-awake, log-once and in-flight-cancel tests. Every negative-control row still passed.
- Also ran:
  - full `go test ./cmd/gc`: ok (444s);
  - `go vet`, `golangci-lint` on the touched packages (0 issues);
  - `make bazel-sync`;
  - `go test ./scripts/cipolicy ./internal/testpolicy/...`.

## Risks / review focus
- A live but wedged claim holder is no longer reclaimed by the orphaned or no-wake/idle drains. Its remaining ways out are the execution-stalled backstop, max-age, operator intent, or the claim bead closing or being re-owned. This is intended (invariant I1). The claim-releasing remedy is part of the v1.6 epic.
- Every orphaned or no-wake-reason/idle drain candidate for a configured pool session now costs one live bd read. Sessions with a stamp cost one more.
- An in-flight **no-wake-reason/idle** drain is not cancelled by the live-claim lens. That lens was deliberately limited to "orphaned" per the approved scope; the veto only prevents such drains from starting. The existing assign [truncated]

PR title: fix(mcp): skip agents on non-MCP harnesses instead of failing city start

PR description:
## Summary

Stage-1 MCP projection (`buildStage1MCPTargets`) resolves every agent and returns the first error. So a single agent whose provider runs on a harness gc cannot write an MCP config for (zcode, kimi, copilot, …) aborted `gc init` for the **whole city**:

```
init: project MCP: agent "glm53": effective MCP requires a supported provider family, got "zcode"
```

Three production cities (platform, substrate, trust) sat in `init_failed` on exactly this, because one provider-derived helper agent inherited the city MCP catalog. Their Slack seats were unreachable for days as a result.

## Changes

- **Clear error.** `resolveAgentMCPProjection` now returns a typed `unsupportedMCPHarnessError` that names the MCP servers, the harness, the supported harnesses, and the fix:
  > MCP servers [notes] are configured for this agent, but its provider runs on the "copilot" harness, which cannot receive MCP (supported harnesses: claude, codex, gemini, opencode, mimocode, cursor); switch the agent to a provider on a supported harness or remove the MCP servers from its scope
- **Skip, don't abort.** `buildStage1MCPTargets` skips an agent with that error, prints a warning, and projects every other agent. The warning is deduped per process, so the supervisor's per-tick stage-1 pass doesn't repeat it every tick.
- **The failure stays visible where it belongs.** That agent's own session start still fails with the same error, which `buildDesiredState` already logs and skips per agent.
- `supportsMCPProviderKind` now reads from one `mcpProviderKinds` list, which the error message also uses.

Other stage-1 errors (target conflicts, workdir resolution, apply failures) still fail as before. Only the harness-capability case is downgraded to a per-agent skip.

## Testing

- New `TestRunStage1MCPProjectionSkipsUnsupportedHarnessAgent`: a city MCP catalog with a gemini agent and a copilot agent. Stage 1 succeeds, the gemini projection is written, the warning names the agent, harness, and servers, and a second tick does not re-warn.
